Title: Digital Services and Resources Librarian

POSITION SUMMARY

The Digital Services and Resources Librarian provides leadership in the management of online library resources, including the library website and electronic resources, and serves as a member of the Reference and Instruction Team. This position has primary responsibility for the library website and the user experience of online library products, including virtual reference tools, discovery tools, and instructional technologies; and ensures that Library services, online resources, and instructional products are pleasurable to use and accessible. This position also manages the life cycle of library databases including selection, procurement, implementation, and annual review. 

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES
Library Website and User Experience
Plans, develops and evaluates the State University Library website; performs updates and revisions to website content; serves as liaison between the Library and the College’s Digital Group
Integrates web-based library products into the library website including the discovery system, electronic resources, virtual reference tools, research guides, forms, blogs, etc. 
In collaboration with the Metadata and Systems Librarian, evaluates, develops, and customizes the library discovery system including the user interface and search scopes to ensure an optimal user experience
Assesses the impact of technology-based services on Library users, including the Library website, discovery system, research guides, and other web-based systems through usability testing and the interpretation of usage statistics and analytics
Reviews the accessibility of online library products and makes updates to ensure their usability for persons with disabilities
Builds library staff awareness of new and emerging technologies and electronic resources; collaborates with Academic Technology to provide support and training to faculty
Electronic Resources
Manages the annual electronic resources cycle including evaluation, budgeting, procurement, implementation, and promotion of databases
Leads the Electronic Resources Committee in the evaluation and selection/deselection of databases; works with liaison librarians to gather database feedback from faculty
Serves as the main library contact with database vendors; works with vendor representatives to set up database trials, obtain price quotes, procure new resources after committee selection, and manage invoices
Works closely with the Assistant to the Library Director to ensure database licenses and invoices are approved through the procurement process established by the Controller’s Office
Works closely with the Metadata and Systems Librarian to ensure electronic resources are accessible through the library catalog, discovery system, authentication system, and link resolvers
Troubleshoots technical problems with user access to electronic resources 
Reference and Instruction
Participates in the information literacy program and in development and delivery of online instructional content and classroom instruction
Works closely with the Instruction and Online Learning Librarian to support development and evaluation of online instructional components
Works closely with the Head of Reference and Instruction to assess and enhance delivery of research services
Creates widgets, videos, modules and other products that embed resources and services into the learning management system
Serves as a library liaison with one or more academic departments.
Responds to reference inquiries and research consultation requests via email, chat, phone, video conferencing software, and/or in-person
QUALIFICATIONS


ALA-accredited MLIS or equivalent degree
General
Minimum of two years of professional experience in an academic library with a thorough understanding of academic user needs
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills with the ability to interact with a diverse group of students, faculty, and staff
Demonstrated effective time management and organizational skills, including the ability to plan and implement projects
Enthusiastic public service orientation and commitment to providing user-centered services  
Experience collaborating to find solutions to workflow and service challenges
Library Website and User Experience
Familiarity with standard practices in web development, usability, and accessibility and experience with usability studies and assessment
Demonstrated skill in implementing HTML/CSS web content
Experience using content management systems, discovery systems, learning management systems, and online collaborative productivity tools
Electronic Resources
Familiarity with a variety of electronic resources and databases
Experience with electronic resources management including the ability to work with database vendors
Demonstrated competency in managing and troubleshooting access to electronic content 
Reference and Instruction
Reference and instruction experience in an academic library including proficiency with information literacy principles and practices
Demonstrated experience developing tutorials or other research and instructional tools
Ability to perform in-depth research and present findings to users 
Ability to learn new software applications, programs, and tools and to assist users with a wide array of applications and technologies 

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
Experience with Alma, Primo VE, and OpenAthens or other discovery and authentication systems
Experience providing instructional technology support 
Familiarity with collection development principles and experience with faculty liaison programs
A working knowledge of copyright, fair use, and open access
Active participation in local, state, or national professional organizations
This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties, or responsibilities required of the employee and is subject to change based on the needs of the department and/or college.
We seek individuals with a demonstrated ability to work with students, faculty, and staff from a wide range of social and cultural backgrounds. All employees are expected to advance the College's DEI mission. For more information on the office of Academic Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion please visit: state.edu/diversity.
 RESUME
SKILLS


Electronic Resource Management
Information Literacy and Instruction
Reference and Research Consultation
User Experience and Usability
Web Design: HTML, CSS
Content Management Systems: 
Drupal, Wordpress, Cascade
3D Printing, 3D Scanning, and Vinyl Cutting
Video Tutorial Creation: Camtasia


EDUCATION


Redwood College, Cedar Park, OH 	 
Master of Library and Information Science	Eastern Ohio University, Athens, OH Bachelor of Science in Psychology, Cum Laude


EXPERIENCE	
State University Library, Capital City, OH 	                      August 2013-present
Digital Services Librarian
Manage the library website (https://library.colum.edu/) and ensure access to electronic resources.
Collaborated with the campus web designer and developer to redesign the library website and migrate content to the college’s content management system in July 2015. 
Conduct periodic usability testing of the library website with students and make iterative changes based on testing. 
Update website content and integrate vendor products including the EBSCO Discovery Service and Springshare’s LibGuides, LibAnswers, and LibCal.
Manage EZproxy authentication including updating of config and patron files.
Troubleshoot online access issues including problems with authentication and broken links. 
As a member of the Electronic Resources Committee, review, select, and deselect databases based on curricular needs and budget constraints. 
Teach information literacy and library resources to undergraduate students during library instruction sessions. 
Lead 20-30 one hour instruction sessions per semester for First Year Writing, Cultural Studies, Entrepreneurship, Management, Photography, and Design Thinking courses.
Correspond with faculty to ensure instruction meets course objectives. 
Serve as library liaison to faculty in the Interactive Arts and Media (DAM), Interdisciplinary Arts, and Humanities departments. 
Attend faculty meetings and correspond via email to promote library resources and services and learn about department needs. 
Write, record, and edit tutorial videos (https://bit.ly/3x9L9aQ) about library resources using Camtasia software; follow accessibility best practices when creating videos. 
Select and deselect books and ebooks for the religion, psychology, and philosophy collections. 
Beginning in September 2019, took over management responsibilities, including training and scheduling,  for two student employees.
Manage the Library Maker Lab.

Teach students to operate the 3D printers, 3D scanners, and vinyl cutter.

Oakridge Public Library, Oakridge, OH 		     November 2011-August 2013
Systems Librarian

Managed an electronic resources budget (excluding ebooks and streaming media) in excess of $300,000 annually. 
Trained library staff and patrons on the use of new resources.
Troubleshot problems with database access and worked with IT to resolve access issues.
Negotiated database pricing with vendors, reviewed all invoices, and ensured timely payment by the business office. 
Conducted a cost-per-use analysis of databases; canceled underperforming databases and selected new databases. 
Advised the IT department about website updates.
Coordinated purchase and implementation of the library mobile app from Boopsie. 
Identified the need for an e-newsletter and coordinated planning and implementation.
Administered the library’s chat reference service through LibraryH3lp. 
Coordinated the library’s social media presence and managed the social media committee.  
Designed adult social media and technology classes and taught at least two classes per month. 
Provided one-on-one instruction or research assistance to patrons through the Book-a-Librarian service.
Responded to reference questions in-person and online at the adult reference desk and teen reference desk. 
Selected and deselected books for the nonfiction science and computer collections.

Redwood College, Cedar Park, OH 			                           September 2010-November 2011
School of Information Science

Maintained and expanded the EMP website including implementing social media.

PROFESSIONAL INVOLVEMENT
Library UX Midwest	October 2017-present
Steering Committee
Attend monthly meetings to plan events and workshops for librarians interested in assessment, user experience, and design thinking. 
On a rotating basis, lead Coffee Chats, an informal networking and discussion series. 

Create @ Your Library		January 2013-present
Co-Founder
With an LEADERS USA grant-funded team, in collaboration with Instructions, developed a website where librarians can search for maker projects and resources. (http://makeitatyourlibrary.org/) 
With a Foundation prototyping grant, expanded from a website to a collection of Maker Kits shared by libraries across Ohio through Interlibrary Loan. Provided kits to the Ohio State Library for administration of delivery. 
 October 8, 2019

Electronic Resources &
Social Sciences Librarian Search Committee
Founder's Memorial Library
Gateway City, OH 43210

To whom it may concern: 

I recently found your job posting for an Digital Resources and Humanities Librarian and I am interested in pursuing this opportunity at the Founder's Memorial Library because I identify strongly with your goal of providing information to the Gateway University community “anytime, anywhere.”

I am well prepared to continue ensuring the students, faculty, and staff at GU have access to the electronic resources they need for their academic and research pursuits. During my time as the Systems Librarian at Oakridge Public Library, I coordinated the library’s collection of databases with a budget of over $300,000.00. In addition managing vendor relationships, I took the initiative to conduct a cost per use analysis based on observations that some of the databases were not being used enough to justify their cost. I reviewed Electronic Resource Management Systems and selected an open access system built on Microsoft Access. After inputting all of the usage data and running the analysis, I made the decision, with input from colleagues, to cancel subscriptions to several databases and selected several new databases that better met the needs of the community. For example, we canceled our subscriptions to an academic level nursing database and added a new consumer health database better suited to the public. 

As the Digital Services Librarian at State University Library, I ensure access to and troubleshoot the electronic resources and EBSCO Discovery System. One major challenge I identified and sought solutions for was the out-of-date EZproxy system. The EZproxy authentication system was hosted on an aging server and the system, managed outside of the library, was not being updated. After several instances of the server going down and students and faculty being unable to access necessary resources, I began looking for alternatives. I made the case for switching to OCLC’s hosted EZproxy and library administration agreed. This eliminated the task of updating the system and servers and gave library staff the ability to directly make changes to the config and user files. I also troubleshoot the majority of access issues - speaking directly with students and faculty about error messages and broken links - and contact vendor support when problems cannot be resolved in-house. 

As part of a small reference and instruction team at State, I work collaboratively and efficiently to provide curricular support in and out of the classroom. In the classroom, I build discussions and activities that draw from the ACRL Framework for Information Literacy for Higher Education. For example, drawing from the Authority is Constructed and Contextual Frame, I often lead a discussion with first year writing students where I invite them to contribute to a list of information sources including magazines, books, articles, blogs, etc. Then together we begin to identify the people or professions that create and contribute to those sources and how or why those sources are used. Out of the classroom, i.e., online, I recently began creating tutorial videos with Camtasia. As part of this effort, I was inspired by a conference presentation to focus on making accessible videos (e.g., high contrast visuals, clear audio with synchronous captions, guiding language, etc.) and created a list of best practices that is used by the instruction team. 

I am committed to keeping abreast of the dynamic and rapid changes technology is bringing to librarianship while never losing sight of core services like instruction and reference. Given my skills and experience, I believe I can be an asset to your library team and look forward to discussing the position with you. Thank you for your time and consideration. 

Sincerely, 

Sarah T. Jenkins
 Evaluation Period
September 1, 2020 -  April 30, 2021

Employee Comments:
Two projects I have begun and, in one case, completed during the evaluation period demonstrate my commitment to high quality in my work: 
In October 2020, I began our migration to a new authentication system, OpenAthens. At this time, I was also preparing for maternity leave and successfully convinced the system vendor (EBSCO) to move up our implementation date from Spring to Fall so that the bulk of the work could be completed before my leave. It was important to begin sooner rather than later because the OpenAthens system provides many benefits over the EZproxy system we have used for many years including better integration with the college’s IT systems, better security, single sign on, and a cost savings over EZproxy. 
In March 2021, I volunteered to re-convene the E-Resources Committee in order to evaluate our current databases and electronic resources and review potential new resources. A systematic review of the library’s electronic resources had not been completed since the Collections Management Librarian left the college and the position was eliminated three years ago. I saw a need for the work to be completed in order to provide students and faculty with the most robust and useful mix of electronic resources possible within the budget allotted. The importance of the library’s electronic resources in support of remote learning due to the pandemic and beyond and made this project even more critical. 

Overall, I strive to maintain a high level of quality in my work and I continually look for ways to improve library services and support student learning. 
I manage the library website and make incremental changes as needed based on input from library staff. For example, on September 3rd, a new search interface was launched which was designed in consultation with the Digital Group. 
I provide virtual information literacy instruction to students and teach students how to utilize library resources for their coursework. This includes the creation of 15 tutorial videos. 
I respond to questions and research inquiries from students and faculty in an accurate and timely manner through our chat and email reference services and through one-one-one research consultations via Zoom.
I troubleshoot authentication and database access issues by communicating with the affected student or faculty via email or chat and when necessary contact the database vendor for support. 
I supervised one library student staff for the reference department until I went on leave in November. Supervision included creating schedules, approving timesheets, training, overseeing student projects, and communicating regularly. 
I periodically make customizations and configuration changes to our new discovery system, Primo VE, based on user feedback and information learned through training sessions. I also work closely with our Catalog Assistant to ensure that resources in the library catalog are displaying and linking correctly in the discovery system.

In addition, I learned new ideas for website evaluations through my attendance at the ACRL conference in April that I plan to implement in the future (see future goals). 

Goal 2: In March 2020, I volunteered to lead the electronic resources committee through a review and evaluation of our current databases and potential new databases. While this was not necessarily what I had in mind when I wrote this goal, our databases and electronic resources are important resources that support student learning and the curriculum of the college. In addition, I have begun reviewing LibGuides, particularly the LibGuides I own, in collaboration with the Instruction and Online Learning Librarian and the Reference Team.

Goal 3: I have attended multiple Primo VE configuration workshops in order to build my knowledge of the system, particularly in learning about the configurations and customizations that are possible. I have made minor changes thus far, but plan to test other changes by using a Primo sandbox and getting feedback from the Web Team. Additionally, I was also recently selected to serve on the CONSORTIUM Primo VE task force which will allow me to collaborate with peers at other institutions to both learn more about Primo VE and share our knowledge with other CONSORTIUM libraries.

Goal 4: Through my work with the e-resources committee, we selected several new databases that support DEI curriculum including HistoryMakers and the Lake Defender Archive Extension. I also create captions for all the tutorial videos I create to make them accessible.

To Whom It May Concern:

I recently found your job posting for a Digital Services and Emerging Technologies Librarian and I am extremely interested in pursuing this opportunity at State University Library because I identify strongly with your teaching mission and your commitment to lifelong learning and artistic expression. 

At Redwood College, I took full responsibility for developing and implementing social media for the School of Information Science (SIS) and the Education Media Program (EMP). I develop themes and generate content for the Facebook pages and Twitter accounts. My postings regularly share the advice and expertise of library professionals and engage students. I also utilize Hootsuite, a social media dashboard, to manage these various social media outlets and schedule postings in advance. As a result of these efforts, the EMP Facebook page has attracted 90 followers in six months and the SIS following has increased to 206. 

Additionally, I have utilized the skills I learned through coursework in reference, including business reference, to complete research requests at the discretion of the PhD Program Director at Redwood. One such request involved locating information about other PhD programs and organizing the information so that key aspects of various programs could be easily compared. In order to resolve these requests successfully, I often follow up with the director after my research is completed. As a result of several years of customer service experience, I am a strong communicator and I feel comfortable asking the questions that will lead me to fully understanding of the needs of the questioner. 

I realize that OPL’s electronic resources are diverse and extensive, but I am poised to tackle the challenge of managing these resources. My interest in and experience working with electronic resources began with graduate coursework in Advanced Web Design. The course taught me how to work with a content management system and how databases function from the inside out. I applied this knowledge while working on several electronic resources during my practicum in the library of the National Civic Association (NCA). NCA was preparing to launch a new web tool. I audited the topics covered by the web tool and recommended additions to the bibliography. I also developed a database for the Kids Books collection and promoted the collection by writing book reviews for an e-newsletter /blog.

I am dedicated to bringing enthusiasm for helping others – from all backgrounds and education levels, from the technophobic to the computer savvy – to your library. I am also inspired to think creatively about the application of social media and emerging technologies at and I look forward to working with library staff to infuse traditional library services with these technologies. I am committed to keeping abreast of the dynamic and rapid changes technology is bringing to librarianship while also never losing sight of traditional and indispensible library services like instruction and reference.

Given my skills and experience, I believe I can be an asset to your library team and look forward to discussing the position with you.  Thank you for your time and consideration.

Sincerely,

Sarah T. Jenkins
